newsitem.title: ITALY: Electronic money needs supervision - BoI official.
newsitem.headline: Electronic money needs supervision - BoI official.

text.p: Payment cards make the global retail payments system more efficient but central banks have a major responsibility in preserving confidence in national currencies, Bank of Italy deputy director general Tommaso Padoa-Schioppa told a banking conference.

The new generation of payment instruments pose a number of problematic issues, he said. First, in consideration of their potentially widespread use they require a degree of confidence comparable to that of traditional instruments.

The features of the schemes could also make them attractive for illegal purposes such as money laundering and tax evasion. Also, the development of the new instruments could have a significant impact on the use of central bank money such as cash and bank reserves, he said.

The global nature of the new products has prompted the central banks of the Group of 10 to cooperate in examining issues pertaining to electronic money, Padoa-Schioppa said, noting that one area in which conclusions had already been drawn by central banks was security.
"A report recently published by the G10 observes that electronic money systems could be designed to incorporate security on a par with other payment instruments," he said.

Central banks are convinced that the new products can improve the efficiency of retail payments and that market forces are the driving force in this area. "The market should play, and does play, the key role. But this does not mean that there is no role for public policy," he said.
"The problem for central banks is to devise an approach that takes into account potential benefits as well as risks, and is, as far as possible, both effective and respectful of the market."

"Since confidence is a public good, it cannot be ensured by market forces alone. This is why the evolution towards more abstract forms of money necessitates new forms of public action by central banks," he added. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
